story:
The name over the door of the hall of making is Meical, and it was the old master's. The one who answers to it now is a drakoran, and the fort's name registrar writes his name in the second book with a mark beside it that means borrowed. What he was called before he came to the hall, nobody in the dales knows. Martley, the only drakoran who ever studied at the colleges, says he never knew him and would have; whoever this is learned his making from the old master's books, alone, after the burning, which Martley thinks is the most dangerous way there is to learn anything.

He came to the empty hall in the first summer of the war, while the colleges were still smoking, and found the master's books on the bench and the servants standing where they had stopped. He read the books. He set the servants going again. He took the name over the door, perhaps because the households kept calling him by it and it was simpler, perhaps because he believed that a man who could read the master's books was the master. He calls himself the cabalist. The households say Master Meical, as they always did, and the servants know better.

They know better and obey worse every year. The Guardian at the stair will not let him up. The Keeper gives him nothing. Tyian ignores his hand at the bench and Pazia keeps him out of the house. When he is troubled in his own hall, no servant of it comes to him; the sentries in their line and the heavy metals in the yard go on with what they were doing. He has the master's books and none of the master's hands.

At the top of the hall stands the lifeless creation, finished in every part but its heart, and below it the orb is broken. Lady Lurlei of Caer Gothwaite says the two are one working: the cabalist means to wake his creation with what the orb held, and the breaking of it is why the wards of Caer Gothwaite part before drakoran craft. Adelon on the hill says the creation is the old master's, the last thing he made, and that the drakoran only finished it. The realm finds out the only way it can. When someone sets a heart in the creation and tries to wake it, the cabalist comes up to the top of his hall to defend it. That is the one thing in the dales he will always come out for.
legend: Cabalist Meical is the level 58 drakoran who runs Meical's Hall in the Dales of Devwy, and he only shows for Restoring the Magic (Lady Lurlei): after you give the orb to the lifeless creation at the top of the hall, he comes to defend it. Kill him, take his box (Pazia's key opens it), read the note, then cleanse the broken orb with the pendant. He is aggressive but has no faction, so none of the hall's constructs come to help him; the sentries and heavy metals nearby can still aggro on you by themselves, so clear the top of the hall first. No spells or styles in the data: a melee fight with a 58, a full group of fifties is comfortable. If you lose him, he is back in about ten minutes.

loremasterTopic.text: The drakoran who answers to the old master's name over the door of the hall of [meical]. He learned the making from the master's books alone after the burning, set the [servants] going again and calls himself the cabalist, but none of them obeys him well and none comes when he calls. At the top of the hall stands the lifeless creation, the master's or his, and below it the [orb] is broken. He comes out to defend the creation, and for nothing else.

bookPage: From a letter of Martley, the only drakoran who studied at the colleges, to the readers at Caer Gothwaite. You ask whether I know the one in the hall of making. I do not, and I would. He learned from the master's books, alone, with nobody to tell him what the master meant and what the master only wrote. That is how a man comes to believe that a name over a door is a name. I have seen him from the hill. He holds out his hand to the servants and they look past it, the way a dog looks past a stranger who calls it by its name. He has not understood why. I think he never will. I think that is why he is making something new.
